items.title: Understanding Geometric Twins
items.explanation: Geometric twins are figures that have the same shape and size, meaning they are congruent. To create an exact replica of a figure, you need specific measurements that fix its shape and size. For example, knowing the lengths of two sides (AB and BC) and the angle between them (∠ABC) allows you to construct an exact copy. Without fixing the angle, different triangles can be formed with the same side lengths, so all three measurements are required for certainty.

items.title: The SSS Congruence Condition
items.explanation: If two triangles have the same sidelengths, they are guaranteed to be congruent. This is known as the Side-Side-Side (SSS) condition. For instance, if you measure three sides of a triangle as 4 cm, 6 cm, and 8 cm, any other triangle with these exact side lengths will be congruent to the original.
